fieldValues.title: Decision checklist: one container, reviewed at every owner session for now
fieldValues.decision_question: Where do we manage what makes a good decision, and how often is it reviewed while it is new?
fieldValues.context: The owner, 2026-11-05 (vignettes 43f236ce and a04e8ab7): 'We need to have a place where we manage our decision checklist. It will need to be reviewed often for a while.' That the place and frequent review are wanted is the owner's; the shape and the stopping rule below are the proposal. Precedent consulted: 7b91246b (gate on a case per option; this holds the content its tests come from), e56d6893 (framing rules as convention first; its four rules become checks here), 7ee8fa01 (a decision is shown with its compass; DC-12 applies it), e337703b (convention before enforcement: the checks start as a convention), 4445b9cf (cite, never re-ask; DC-08). Tension: Reviewable and fast.
fieldValues.friction: The checks are scattered, so nobody can tell which version applies, and a low-effort review changes nothing. Frequent review costs session time, in the one place this programme is trying to take load off (SP-113).
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
A. Do nothing: the checks stay in the handbook, e56d6893, semanticops.com#37 and the muDemocracy guide. Leads to: the same decisions, the owner keeps clicking recommended.
B. A handbook section. Leads to: one readable page; each change is a clerk PR; no evidence per check and nothing puts it on an agenda.
C. One record holding the whole list. Leads to: simple and reviewable, but evidence and retirement cannot attach to a single check.
D. One record per check in a container, with an open exercise in the decision log that puts the review on every session's agenda (chosen). Leads to: each check changes alone; no new code; fifteen records to keep.
E. D, reviewed only at the monthly retrospective. Leads to: less session load, and slow learning while the list is most likely wrong.
fieldValues.key_requirements: One home the handbook and tools cite, not restate. Review reaches the owner without anyone remembering to raise it. Review stops when it stops changing things.
fieldValues.decision_statement: We manage the decision checklist in one container of per-check records, reviewed at every owner session until three reviews in a row change nothing.
fieldValues.rationale: D over B and C because the point of frequent review is to change single checks on evidence, which needs each check addressable. D costs no code because an open exercise in the decision log already appears on every session's agenda. D over E because the list is untested on our own decisions, and the owner asked for frequent review while it is new.
fieldValues.revisit_when: Not working: the owner holds or skips the review at two sessions running, or the list grows past 15 checks with none retired. Done its job: three reviews in a row change nothing; then the exercise closes and the checks are reviewed at the retrospective.
fieldValues.next_steps: Session review through exercise in container 871b27f9; the clerk issue on the checklist makes the handbook, briefs and pr-check cite it.
